data.name: Jaswant
data.gender_notes: Jaswant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Jaswant is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘jas’ which means ‘desirable’ and ‘want’ which means ‘to wish’. The name is often given to a child as a symbol of the parents' hope and desire for their child's future happiness and success. The name Jaswant carries the meaning “Desirable, Wish-fulfilling” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jaswant usually hope their child will grow to embody desirable, wish-fulfilling and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the parents' deepest wishes and desires for their child.
data.etymology: Jaswant belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Desirable, Wish-fulfilling.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jaswant total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jaswant holds great cultural significance in Hindu culture, especially in North India, where it is commonly used. It represents the parents' highest hopes and aspirations for their child's future. The name carries the weight of expectations, as they believe that the child will grow up to be a gleaming embodiment of all things desirable and worthy of their deepest wishes.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Jaswant is believed to represent the divine gift of desire, which is a fundamental aspect of human life. The name encourages the child to cultivate and nurture their desires, as they are a powerful force in shaping their destiny. The name also serves as a reminder of the importance of living in accordance with the Divine Will, as the truest source of allDesirable things and the deepest source of inner fulfillment.
